subject: Recap + procurement readiness: Redwood trial & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + next steps: Redwood trial & procurement path

Hi Alice —

Thanks again for taking the time today to run through your use cases and traffic profile. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

- What we heard: real-time summarization for customer support (high qps, 512 context), batch indexing for search relevance (embeddings), and a small set of higher-quality assistant flows.
- Trial ask: 2-week sandbox to validate latency and cost at 50k tokens/day.
- Procurement note (ACTION): we need to confirm how ACME will purchase (PO via SAP vs. corporate card vs. marketplace). Also want to confirm who handles contract review and expected timeline.

Proposed next steps:
1) I’ll send a draft quote & sample SOW (line-itemed for committed vs burst). Attached will be pricing assuming dedicated capacity + burst credits.
2) Can you confirm procurement contact & whether ACME prefers a PO (SAP) or payment by card? If marketplace is preferred (AWS/Azure), let me know — that changes invoicing.
3) Dev happy to join a procurement call; can we tentatively book a 30‑minute sync next week if needed?

If you’re comfortable, can you introduce me to the procurement contact or forward their process checklist? That’ll help us avoid surprises.

Thanks —

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

From: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Jul 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps: Redwood trial & procurement path

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the summary — that looks right from our side. A few clarifications: 

- Procurement at ACME is handled through SAP and we typically issue a PO. We do not usually pay by corporate card for arrangements over $10k.
- Procurement contact: Bob Lee (bob.lee@acme.com) — I’m cc’ing procurement so they have context.
- Marketplace: we prefer to use marketplace purchases where possible, but this deal may need to be on-contract (vendor invoice + PO) depending on the SOW. Can you confirm if Redwood supports both marketplace and direct vendor invoicing?
- Timeline: we’re aiming to have a sandbox in place by end of July, pending legal review and budget signoff.

Can you send the line‑itemed quote and SOW when ready and we’ll route to our procurement/legal teams.

Best,
Alice
Alice Johnson
Director, Product — Search & Assist
ACME Corporation
alice.johnson@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Jul 2026 11:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps: Redwood trial & procurement path

Hi Alice —

Great — thanks for the clarity. Attached are:
- Redwood-Quote-ACME-0626.pdf (line‑itemed: committed capacity, burst credits, and optional observability add-on)
- ACME_SOW_v1.pdf (sample SOW with success criteria and acceptance steps)

Short answers: yes — we support both marketplace purchases (AWS & Azure) and direct vendor invoicing with PO. Marketplace purchases simplify billing but can limit contract customization; direct invoicing + PO gives full contract flexibility (SLA, data terms). Happy to map the differences in a short note for procurement/legal.

A couple of asks to speed the path: 
- Can Bob confirm the PO process lead time (typical SOW review cadence) and any internal form the legal team needs filled?
- If you can share a preferred order number format (or a POC PO), we’ll ensure the quote maps to your chart of accounts.

I’m happy to join a 30‑minute procurement sync next week with Dev (solutions) to walk through the attached and answer technical questions. Proposed times: Tue 7/7 10:00–10:30 or Thu 7/9 14:00–14:30 PT. Which works best for the team?

Thanks —

Marissa

Attachments: Redwood-Quote-ACME-0626.pdf, ACME_SOW_v1.pdf

From: Bob Lee <bob.lee@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 06 Jul 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + procurement readiness: Redwood trial & next steps

Marissa / Alice —

Thanks for the context. Procurement is reviewing the SOW but we have two open items from finance:

1) We need the final quote with explicit yearly and monthly line items (committed tokens, burst units, observability add-on) for our budget owner.
2) CFO wants to see a breakdown between subscription (recurring) and one‑time professional services.

Where is the final quote (the quote attached looks like a draft)? Also, our internal approval is paused pending confirmation of the ownership of data retention terms in the SOW — legal flagged that.

If you can provide a final quote with the requested breakdown and a short note on data retention policy (or point us to the standard terms), we’ll move to PO creation.

Bob Lee
Procurement Manager
ACME Corporation
bob.lee@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Bob Lee <bob.lee@acme.com>, Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + procurement readiness: Redwood trial & next steps

Thanks Bob — appreciate the specific asks. Quick check‑in and plan to unblock: 

- I’ll circulate a final quote with explicit yearly/monthly line items (committed vs burst) and a separate row for professional services by EOD Wednesday 7/8.
- Dev will include a short technical note on data retention and where that’s captured in our standard terms; I’ll also attach the Redwood data retention summary.
- If procurement prefers, we can provide a marketplace purchase order template (AWS/Azure) or direct vendor invoice — whichever shortens your internal flow.

To keep momentum, would you be open to a 15‑minute weekly check‑in on Fridays at 10:00am PT to quickly surface blockers until the PO is issued? If yes, I’ll send a recurring invite.

If anything is stuck on our side, please flag the exact blocker (legal clause, ordering account, or line item) and I’ll escalate internally.

Thanks —

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198
